findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O failure (missing file, permission denied, truncated UTF-8).
findings.failure_mode: Hostile or absent file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O or parse error.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and propagate fs::read_to_string errors with map_err to a typed LoadError::Io variant.

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a side-effecting I/O call fused inside the parsing loop.
findings.failure_mode: Breaks functional core purity: the function produces observable side effects that cannot be controlled or suppressed by callers, and makes testing/determinism impossible.
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely. If logging is required, pass a logging callback or write events in the shell layer outside load_metrics.

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] accessed via unchecked indexing without verifying parts.len() >= 2.
findings.failure_mode: A line missing a comma, an empty line, or a line with only one field triggers a panic at runtime instead of returning a typed parse error.
findings.fix: Check parts.len() >= 2 (or use split_once to get exactly two parts) and return a typed ParseError for malformed lines.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric content in the value field.
findings.failure_mode: Malformed numeric data aborts the program. Combined with the unchecked indexing above, a single bad line crashes the entire load.
findings.fix: Use .map_err to convert parse errors into a typed ParseError variant and propagate through Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>.

findings.problem: (...) as u16 is a lossy cast from u32 parsed result to u16. Values 65536 and above silently truncate.
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 in range [65536, u32::MAX] silently wraps to an incorrect u16, corrupting data without any error indication.
findings.fix: Use .try_into().map_err(|_| ParseError::ValueOutOfRange) or explicitly check value <= u16::MAX before casting.

findings.problem: load_metrics has no domain cap on the number of lines/records. A large file allocates unboundedly.
findings.failure_mode: An attacker or misconfiguration can supply a multi-gigabyte file, causing OOM kill or sustained memory pressure.
findings.fix: Add a MAX_RECORDS constant, enforce it during iteration (e.g., take(MAX_RECORDS) or checked_count), and return a typed error when exceeded.

findings.problem: let parts: Vec<String> = line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a Vec of Strings for each line, but only parts[0] and parts[1] are used.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation per line. For fixed two-field lines this is wasteful; for many lines it compounds memory pressure.
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to get exactly two &str parts, trim them, and construct Record without intermediate Vec<String>.

findings.problem: Record fields are pub (name: String, value: u16), exposing internal representation and allowing invalid construction from outside the module.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can create Record instances with empty names or invalid values, bypassing the single parse boundary at load_metrics.
findings.fix: Make fields private, add a smart constructor Record::new(name: String, value: u16) -> Result<Self, RecordError>, and export only valid instances.

findings.problem: load_metrics returns Vec<Record> with no error type. All failure modes are swallowed by unwrap.
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot distinguish between file-not-found, I/O errors, malformed lines, out-of-range values, or domain-cap breaches. No recovery or retry strategy is possible.
findings.fix: Define enum LoadError { Io(std::io::Error), Parse(ParseError), TooManyRecords } and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>.

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for load_metrics. The function creates per-line Vec<String> allocations and calls println! inside the hot loop.
findings.failure_mode: Performance characteristics are unknown. The hidden I/O in the parsing loop makes it impossible to benchmark the pure computation separately from side effects.
findings.fix: Add a criterion/cargo-bench benchmark that measures parsing throughput with and without the hidden println, and document allocation counts with allocators or a profiling run.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_metrics parsing throughput
no profiler evidence for per-line allocation patterns
no allocation audit (e.g., #[global_allocator] stats or criterion benchmarks) for unbounded file loading
no command evidence that cargo fmt/check/clippy/test pass (static review only, no commands run per instructions)
residual_risk: Static review only. No commands were run per task instructions (cargo commands forbidden). The code has 6 BLOCKER violations: unwrap on I/O and parse, unchecked indexing, lossy u32-to-u16 cast, hidden println! side effect in core, no domain cap on allocations, and no typed error taxonomy. All unwrap calls are reachable by hostile input (missing file, malformed CSV lines, non-numeric values, values exceeding u16::MAX, oversized files).
